notes.title: Spaceslingers has Launched!
notes.content:
Spaceslingers is now available!

Firstly, let's dive right into the rundown of the game!
[hr][/hr]Spaceslingers is a space-time bending interstellar ride requiring careful use of gravity and time dilation to navigate through interstellar hazards and land on a target planet, delivering your payload with the lowest possible time taken.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38354692/7d0a2eb72ddea895d448b4513b00b314cb7e781b.png[/img]
 
Featuring bizarre cosmic objects, both real and imagined, like blackholes, whiteholes and wormholes, you control the direction and power of your ships launch and then let gravity do the rest. By skimming close to space-time warping objects, the time you experience slows down, allowing you to top the leader-boards by being the most daring and risking life and limb skimming event horizons, all in the name of delivering packages for your employer, Spamazon!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38354692/712aa2930946510edba4d4a7b89bb7f7aa77811c.gif[/img]

With over 50 deliveries and an in-built delivery editor allowing you to create custom levels, the potential for cosmic couriers is endless. Just try not to get spaghettified on the way!
[hr][/hr]Now for something a little more personal.

It's been a long road for me, developing this title. What started out as a little prototype of me throwing blocks around a circle that I had coded gravity into has finally morphed into an actual game! A game that people can play! I'm excited and nervous for it to be finally live.

In many ways, it's quite emotional. I started making the game because I have a deep and abiding love of the universe in all its glory. I wanted to make something that was interesting and showed some potential aspects of the universe that people might not be aware of, like time dilation, or the concept of whiteholes. I loved the idea of toying with gravity and it was a lot of fun to see how real-world Newtonian physics interacted in the various situations I concocted.

Making the game has been my life and soul for many months now. There's something akin to loss that comes with finally releasing it. I've still got updates coming and I will be actively working on it for a while yet (and helping people with any bugs/problems they might encounter for the rest lifetime of the game), but this is the culmination, the pinnacle, the apex of the development. My baby is out in the wild now!

I hope that everyone who plays it has fun! I hope to see [u][b]your[/b][/u] name at the top of the leaderboards! And I hope it inspires a little bit more love and fascination with space, astronomy and all the cool things that are as yet undiscovered in our vast, wonderful and mildly terrifying universe!

If you like Spaceslingers and want to see what I'll be working on next, head on over to [url=https://refreshertowel.games]https://refreshertowel.games[/url]!

notes.title: Spaceslingers Demo Ending
notes.content:
Hey folks, I'm going to be taking the Spaceslingers demo down in the next few days, so if you want to give it a go, make sure to download and play it soon!

I was originally intending to take it down on the day the Steam Autumn Games Festival ended. However, I ran into some massive computer issues and totally lost access to all my accounts and computer for nearly a week. It was quite a frustrating experience.

That said, I've gotten everything back now and I'm able to get back on schedule, which means that I'll be removing the demo around two days from now. I'm giving a little bit of leeway so that anyone who is interested in playing it can download it and give it a go (or if you've already downloaded but haven't played, you have some time to play it).

It was a lot of fun seeing the battle for high scores that went on while the demo was up! The full game is nearing completion and will be coming out soon, so don't worry, you'll be able to get your fix of competitive spacetime warping once it gets released!

notes.title: Spaceslingers Live-Stream!
notes.content:
Hey everyone, I'm RefresherTowel, the solo dev making Spaceslingers, and this is a livestream for the Steam Game Festival Autumn Edition.

If you have no idea what Spaceslingers is, here's the rundown: 

[quote]Spaceslingers is a fun and mind-bending 2D sci-fi gravity based game, where the only obstacles between you and your goal are the most powerful objects in the known universe!

Use the gravity wells created by black holes (and other exotic celestial objects) to slingshot your delivery ship to target planets. Easy to play but hard to master, Spaceslingers is filled with both meditative moments of intuition-based planning and jaw-clenching moments of tense action.[/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38354692/2394c4c0dc4362770b3d77d1d2ec8c027b0fc9b0.gif[/img]

The game is a passion project I've been working on for awhile now. It started out because I'm pretty obsessed with space and wanted to see if I could program some cool 2D black holes and it then ballooned into what it is now, a satirical take on corporations forcing underpaid workers to deliver inconsequential packages while facing the harshest environments in the universe...

So if you have any interest at all in physics, astronomy, and the wildly destructive things that exist (or might exist) out there in the universe, then this is definitely a game you want to try.

I'll be taking any questions anyone has, working on some deliveries in the built-in Delivery Editor that comes with the demo (and the full game) and also attempting to beat all the high scores set by players so far...See if you can beat me by playing alongside me during the event!
